topic: Sponsor, vessel identity, and deployment timeline
wiki_text: On 2025-10-28, Excelerate Energy executed a definitive commercial agreement with a subsidiary of Iraq's Ministry of Electricity to build, and operate under a 5-year regasification-services + LNG-supply arrangement, Iraq's first LNG import terminal at the Port of Khor Al Zubair. Guaranteed regasification capacity is 500 MMscf/d (design capacity up to 1,000 MMscf/d); minimum contracted offtake is 250 MMscf/d; total project investment is ~$450 million. Excelerate will deploy its newest FSRU, then known as 'Hull 3407' (built at HD Hyundai Heavy Industries, Ulsan, South Korea; 170,000 m3 storage), officially named 'Excelerate Acadia' at a naming ceremony on 2026-03-31. Due to Iraq-side delays (government payment failures tied to 2026 regional-conflict/Strait-of-Hormuz risk, and an intervening change of Iraqi Prime Minister), Excelerate instead deployed the Excelerate Acadia to Jordan's Aqaba LNG terminal under a 9-month charter with NEPCO beginning ~April/May 2026, while the Iraq project remains delayed. Iraq approved an initial $48 million payment to Excelerate around May/July 2026 to allow berth-modification work to proceed.

topic: Project oversight and structure (fixed platform, not floating)
wiki_text: Iraq's Cabinet appointed South Gas Company (SGC) -- a Ministry of Oil subsidiary headquartered at Khor Al-Zubair, Basrah, and 51% owner of Basrah Gas Company (JV with Shell 44%/Mitsubishi 5%) -- to oversee construction of a fixed (non-floating) regasification platform at Grand Al-Faw Port, reported in Oct-Dec 2024. KBR was separately contracted (via Iraq's Ministry of Planning) for organizational/contractual project-management support, distinct from an EPC or ownership role. A tender for the fixed platform was confirmed launched in March 2025; no contract award or construction-start has been found as of 2026-07. This is a separate project from the Excelerate-backed Khor Al-Zubair FSRU (T100001048168) -- multiple 2025-2026 sources describe Iraq as pursuing 'two new LNG terminals' at these two distinct sites.
